item.title: Introduction to Advanced Movement in IWBTG Fangames
item.description:
This is a short intro into some more advanced movement techniques in fangames. Making this because for me personally, finding how a lot of this stuff worked took a while and required going through a bunch of 10+ year old youtube videos and forum posts.

Things You Already Probably Know

Basic Controls

Use the left and right arrow keys to move around, shift to jump, z to shoot. Press shift again while in the air to double jump.

Water

Water controls the same as usual but you fall slower and have infinite double jump as long as you’re submerged.

Platforms

Platforms are half a block tall and you can pass through them from below. Passing through a platform also regenerates your double jump.

Vines

Of the “main” gameplay mechanics, these were the most counterintuitive to understand at first. To “stick to” a vine, you need to jump towards the wall the vine is on and keep holding down shift even as you’re on the wall. Now when you press the arrow key opposite to the wall you’re on, you jump without spending your double jump. When I first started playing I would just press shift every time I wanted to jump off a vine and get confused on why I was losing my double jump.

Jumping

Fangames generally run at 50 fps and player input is tied to framerate. Depending on how many frames you hold shift down, you will go higher. The maximum height you can reach on your first jump is a 23-frame jump and the max height of your doublejump is 19frames. On a lot of keyboards the shortest jump you can reasonably input is the 2 frame jump however 1 frame jumps are possible using jump cancelling, which I’ll talk about later.

Alignments

Horizontal Aligns

The Kid moves 3 pixels per second, but his hitbox is 11 pixels wide, and blocks are 32 pixels wide. By running into a wall, you can make the kid move 1 or 2 pixels, changing the way you are aligned to the world. Some jumps in certain locations can be impossible if you don’t have the right align, and in general it’s always easier to jump with correct aligns. There are charts online on the best aligns for certain jumps, but in practice most of the time you’ll probably end up running into random walls before jumping or copying somebody else’s aligns from a youtube video. As a rule of thumb the best practice is to find the align that lets you get as close as possible to the spike. Here’s a graphic I found online for best aligns for common jump types.

Vertical Aligns

These are even more confusing and they don’t really matter much for a majority of fangames, but basically the kid’s y position is a floating point value, and with the way gravity is calculated, there is some subpixel remainder that can affect your next jump once you land. There are some methods of getting valigns consistently that fall beyond the scope of this introductory piece but I figured I should still mention them on the topic of aligns.

Vertical Pixel Strings

Because the game runs at 50 fps and collisions/movement are calculated on a discrete frame-by-frame basis, the height at which you fall from can determine whether you get hit by something or not (since your hitbox may not ever technically be colliding). To understand this better, check out the gif below

As you can see, despite hugging the wall in all 3 instances, only the 2 block high drop allows you to fall through without hitting the spike.

Jump Cancelling

You probably have 2 shift keys on your keyboard, meaning if you hold down one of them and release it the moment you press the other, you can trick the game into performing a 1 frame jump. However this can be difficult to use as the timing is strict. You can even chain jump cancels together binding more than 2 shift keys but that goes beyond the scope of this basic intro.

Numpad Cancelling

Due to the weird way shift reacts with the numpad keys, you can actually do 1-frame jumps much easier by:

  1. Pressing and holding shift to start jumping
  2. Instead of releasing shift to end your jump, press a numpad key instead
  3. Keep holding the numpad key and release shift at the moment you want to do the 1frame jump

It takes a bit of getting used to, and you’re unable to change directions while doing it but in general numpad cancelling can help a lot with certain kinds of jumps

AutoHotKey

Depending on your keyboard it can be tricky to reach one of the numpad keys. What I did was make a script using AutoHotKey (a program that lets you remap keys and more) to bind my up arrow key to numpad 0. (Note that rebinding numpad keys can act weird so play around with it before leaving it a certain way.)

Bunnyhopping

Bunnyhopping is when you jump on the exact frame you’ve landed on the floor in a way that can let you get a slightly higher jump right afterwards.

Common Jumps

To finish off this post, I wanna go over the names and strategies for some of the common jump types you’ll see.

Diagonals

Probably the most common type of jump. Not much to say except Jump Through It Lol.

Corners

Corners are also very common. You’ll get used to them but align matters more than for diagonals. Especially for ground corners like the one in the image, the wrong align straight up won’t allow you to jump past.

Gate

Just use a 4 or 5 frame jump to get through.

Diamond

Two gates right next to each other, called a diamond because of the shape formed in the negative space between the spikes. Jump past the first set of spikes and “dip” between the middle of the bottom spikes, then do a 2 or 3 frame jump, or alternatively just numpad cancel through it.

Double Diamond

A very tricky jump. There are a few ways to pass, but I personally find the most consistent way is by doing a 5 frame jump followed by a 2 frame jump as you get really close to the middle spike.

Planes

These jumps are also very precise. However there is a nice strat for the 2-block high plane jump, where if you align yourself on the wall to the left, you can simply hold right and jump until you get past the left spike and use your double jump to clear it.

So yeah, that’s my intro to some fangames concepts, hope ya found this helpful!

item.title: No, We're Not That Stupid
item.description:
Ok so I saw this tweet earlier today and while simple I think it encapsulates the ragebait landscape we’re in extremely well.

At a glance this sounds extremely concerning. I mean come on, they’re literally called ‘potato chips’. Normally this sort of thing doesn’t phase me but this was especially stupid so I felt the need to dig a bit deeper, so I found the FORTUNE article mentioned.

Pay attention to the loaded language in the title. It’s a drastic rebrand after a disturbing finding. All the emphasis is put on the 42% statistic even though that’s a tiny part of the article. But hey, we’ve found out that only Lay’s consumers are stupid idiots, not all consumers in general. That’s an improvement.

But wait. This article wasn’t even written for FORTUNE! It was originally published on Morning Brew. Let’s see what that article looks like.

This title fits the content of the article far better. The whole point is that Lays is rebranding to put more emphasis on being natural. All FORTUNE did was repost the article with a worse clickbait title. But one thing is still bugging me. What is the source for that 2021 study? I tried googling Lays surveys conducted in 2021, but all I got was stuff about flavor preferences, so it must be some internal thing. Whatever.

Anyways, here’s the kicker. I found the story on Pepsico’s website (not linked by FORTUNE or MorningBrew mind you). Let’s check that out.

Yeah can’t fit that one on a single page. The whole thing is basically a PR piece describing why and how they’re implementing their redesign. But don’t fret! Our 42% statistic shows up again.

…

42% of people don’t realize that LAYS chips are made with REAL, FARM GROWN potatoes. Now the actual survey still isn’t given but this phrasing implies something FAR more reasonable than almost half the population being mouthbreathers. 42% of people thought that Lays chips were made of some chemical slop designed to taste like potatoes rather than actual potatoes. (Hey, it even ties back into the theme of attempting to rebrand as more natural!)

This little graphic I slapped together in 3 minutes can hopefully help you see how absurd the tweet is now. A tiny remark in the original story, misconstrued in another article, with a clickbait title slapped on top, followed by a tweet uncritically referencing it while somehow giving even less information.

So there you have it. The journey of an unsubstantiated statistic from a generic corporate PR piece to another nugget of ragebait that’ll be used to make fun of [guy i disagree with] for 2 days before swiftly being forgotten. If you enjoyed this, stick around! I plan on writing posts here more regularly (I say as I wrap up the first real post on this site lol).

item.title: MTH411 Chapter 1 Notes
item.description:
using this mainly as a test to see how latex looks

Sample Spaces

  • The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment is the sample space S
  • Individual outcomes are called points
  • The set of all subsets is called the power set P(S)

Events

  • An event is said to occur if the outcome belongs to the event
  • An event E is the subset of another event F if when E happens, F also happens
  • An event is called the intersection of events if it occurs only when both events occur simultaneously
  • Likewise, an event is the union if at least one of them occurs
  • Complement: everything outside of E
  • Difference: If in E-F, it means it is both in E and not in F
  • Certain: Always happens
  • Impossible: Never happens
  • Mutual exclusivity: Intersection is empty set

Laws

  • Commutative, Associative, Distributive
  • De Morgan:
    • (EUF)c=EcFc
    • (EF)c=EcUFc

Axioms of Probability

Let S be the sample space of a random phenomenon. Suppose that to each event A of S, a number denoted by P(A) is associated with A. If P satisfies the following axioms, then it is called a probability and the number P(A) is said to be the probability of A.

Axiom 1

  • P(A) ≥ 0. The probability of any event is >= 0

Axiom 2

  • P(S)=1. The probability of the sample space is 1

Axiom 3

  • If {A1, A2, A3,…} is a sequence of mutually exclusive events (i.e., the joint occurrence of every pair of them is impossible $$ P\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^\infty A_i\right) = \sum_{i=1}^\infty P(A_i). $$Note that the axioms of probability are a set of rules that must be satisfied before S and P can be considered a probability model.

Odds

Odds are an alternative way of expressing probability. “2 to 1 odds” means 2/3 chance, “x to y odds” means x/(x+y)

Selection from Interval

A point is said to be randomly selected from an interval (a, b) if any two subintervals of (a, b) that have the same length are equally likely to include the point. The probability associated with the event that the subinterval (α, β) contains the point is defined to be (β − α)/(b − a).

The probability of selecting a specific value is 0.
